What are Groups?

A group combines several members of a dimension into one category so the combination can be analysed as a single unit. Groups are built from the data pane, or straight from a visual, and the result behaves like a new dimension — here it is named Purpose (group), State (group) and so on.

Q: What are Groups?
A: A Group is used to combine multiple dimension members into a single category for easier analysis. Groups can be created manually by selecting members, from the data pane, or directly in a visualization. For example, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu and Kerala can be grouped as South India.

Measure Group — Interest Rate Bands

Measures can be grouped too: a continuous measure is bucketed into ranges, then analysed as a band. Loans are grouped by interest rate here.

Measure Group — DTI Bands

The same technique applied to debt-to-income: loans grouped into DTI ranges.
